    People also ask
    What are the 11 ASEAN countries?
    An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
    AI Overview
    As of October 2025, the 11 ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) member countries are Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam, and Timor-Leste (East Timor). Timor-Leste was officially recognized as the 11th member following its expected accession, joining the initial 10 member states in the bloc. 
    The 11 ASEAN Countries: 
    1. Brunei Darussalam (Joined: Jan 7, 1984)
    2. Cambodia (Joined: Apr 30, 1999)
    3. Indonesia
      (Founder member; Joined: Aug 8, 1967)
    4. Laos (Lao PDR) (Joined: Jul 23, 1997)
    5. Malaysia (Founder member; Joined: Aug 8, 1967)
    6. Myanmar (Burma) (Joined: Jul 23, 1997)
    7. Philippines (Founder member; Joined: Aug 8, 1967)
    8. Singapore (Founder member; Joined: Aug 8, 1967)
    9. Thailand (Founder member; Joined: Aug 8, 1967)
    10. Vietnam (Joined: Jul 28, 1995)
    11. Timor-Leste (East Timor) (Accepted as 11th member in 2025) 
    The association aims to promote regional economic growth, social progress, and political stability among its members. The Secretariat is based in Jakarta, Indonesia.

      AI Overview
      The Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) has ten member countries: Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, and Vietnam, with Timor-Leste being the newest member (joining in 2025). These nations collaborate on economic, political, security, and socio-cultural issues, aiming for regional integration and stability, with the Secretariat based in Jakarta, Indonesia.
       
      Founding Members (1967): Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, and Thailand. 
      Later Members: 
      • Brunei Darussalam: (1984)
      • Vietnam: (1995)
      • Laos & Myanmar: (1997)
      • Cambodia: (1999)
      • Timor-Leste: (2025)

        Purpose. What is the purpose of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations?

        AI Overview
        The purpose of ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) is to foster economic growth, social progress, and cultural development while ensuring regional peace and stability, acting as a framework for cooperation in political, economic, and socio-cultural fields among its ten member countries. Its core aims include promoting free trade, strengthening security, improving living standards, and enhancing collaboration in education, science, and technology, all within a framework of respect for justice and the UN Charter.
         
        Key Objectives & Functions:
        • Economic Integration: Accelerating economic growth, improving trade, and creating a single market through initiatives like free trade agreements. 
        • Political & Security Cooperation: Promoting regional peace, stability, and adherence to the rule of law, with platforms for dialogue on security issues. 
        • Socio-Cultural Development: Enhancing quality of life, education, human resource development, and cultural exchange. 
        • Community Building: Working towards an ASEAN Community with three pillars: the Political-Security Community, Economic Community, and Socio-Cultural Community. 
        • Regional Centrality: Acting as a central player in regional forums and a model for cooperation, as seen in its dialogue with major powers like the US, China, and the EU. 
        In essence, ASEAN aims to create a prosperous, peaceful, and integrated Southeast Asian community through joint efforts and partnership.

          AI Overview
          ASEAN's key achievements include fostering regional peace and stability, driving significant economic growth and integration (like the ASEAN Economic Community & RCEP), and creating platforms for political dialogue and cooperation, overcoming post-colonial distrust to build a united bloc with increasing global economic clout. It successfully established frameworks for free trade (AFTA), facilitated the movement of goods/people, and managed complex regional security through forums like the ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF). 
          Political & Security Achievements
          • Peace & Stability: Transformed a conflict-ridden region into one of relative peace, reducing interstate tensions through dialogue. 
          • Diplomatic Forums: Created the ASEAN Regional Forum (ARF) for security dialogue and the Treaty of Amity and Cooperation (TAC) for peaceful relations, endorsed by many non-ASEAN nations. 
          • Cohesive Framework: Established the ASEAN Community (Economic, Political-Security, Socio-Cultural) in 2015, providing structure for deeper integration. 
          Economic Achievements
          • Economic Integration: Launched the ASEAN Free Trade Area (AFTA) and the ASEAN Economic Community (AEC) to create a single market and production base. 
          • Major Trade Partner: Grew into a significant global trading bloc with strong intra-regional trade, fostering collective GDP growth. 
          • Digital & Trade Agreements: Moving towards digital economy governance (DEFA) and participating in massive trade deals like the RCEP (Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership). 
          Regional & Global Influence
          • Model for Regionalism: Became a successful model for regional cooperation among diverse nations. 
          • Geopolitical Voice: Developed the ASEAN Outlook on the Indo-Pacific (AOIP) to promote constructive engagement, not confrontation, in the region. 
          • Poverty Reduction: Contributed to significant economic growth, lifting millions out of poverty.

            Official Languages. What are the official languages of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations?
            About this result
            Feedback
            An AI Overview is not available for this searchCan't generate an AI overview right now. Try again later.
            AI Overview
            The official working language of ASEAN (Association of Southeast Asian Nations) is English, designated by the ASEAN Charter for official communication and meetings, serving as a neutral lingua franca across the diverse linguistic region, though debates exist about adding a secondary regional language like Malay. 
            Why English?
            • Neutrality:
              English avoids privileging any single member state's national language, preventing divisions and maintaining unity. 
            • Functionality:
              It serves as a practical bridge language for diverse member nations with over 1,000 languages spoken within the region. 
            Other Languages in ASEAN:
            • ASEAN promotes national languages and cultures, with member states having their own official languages (e.g., Malay, Indonesian, Thai, Vietnamese, Tagalog, Khmer, Burmese). 
            • While English is for ASEAN business, countries like Singapore and the Philippines use English alongside their national languages (Malay, Mandarin, Tamil in Singapore; Filipino in the Philippines). 
            In essence, English is the common administrative language, while the rich tapestry of local languages defines the region's cultural identity.

              The Association of Southeast Asian Nations is a regional grouping of all 11 states in Southeast Asia, which aims to promote economic and security cooperation among its members. Together, its member states represent a population of more than 680 million people and a land area of over 4.5 million km².
              Source: Wikipedia
